THE CRITICAL STUDY OF THE TAITTIRIYA ARANYAKA AND AN ENGLISH TRANSLATION OF THE TEXT

TRIBHUWAN LAL

BANARAS HINDU UNIVERSITY

1958

Ph.D. (865)

2

[[P002]]

Preface

Aranyakas deserve high place in Indien Philosophy and Vedic studies. The Taittiriya Aranyaka is an important one; but it has not been studied critically in the modern world.

Aranyakas of the

Rgveda Aitareya and sankhayana or Kausitaki have been translated by the famous writer Prof. A.B. Keith; Brhadaranyaka of the white Yajurveda has been also translated by J. Eggeling, the learned translator of the Satapatha Brahmana; but the Taittiriya Aranyaka has not even been translated. This is a very lengthy Aranyaka having many difficult and obscure passages as well as many beautiful passages which threw abundant light on the philosophy, history, society and culture of ancient India. So many words of this Arenyske have not come in any dictionary and Bloomfield has not noted many passages of this Aranyaka in his vedio Concordance. astonished why this excellent Aranyaka has been neglected in this modern age. This is why I took it for my Research. I believe that the critical study and the translation of this Aranyaka will be a great contribution to our knowledge of Indology.

item.title: १ Introduction
item.description:
[[P007]]

1. What is Aranyaka

1

Historical Back-ground:

The Vedic Literature has been divided into three parts:

(1) Samhitas or Mantras, (2) Brahmanes, (3) Aranyakas and Upanisads. Aranyakas, including the Upanisads in them, are the concluding portions of the Vedas. Samhitas contain Mantras, praises and prayers; Brahmanas contain voluminous details for sacrifices; Aranyakas meditate the mystery of the sacrifices; and the Upanisads present the highest philosophy.

The Little Summary

The contents of the Prapathak as in brief:-

The first Prapathaka contains the Mantras and the Brahman as of the Arunake tuka fire-piling.

The second Prapathake deals with the Upavite, Kusmanda Homa (Prayascittas), Vedic study, Brahma sacrifice, interruption of study and five gre et sacrifices'.

In the third Prapathaka there are the Mantras of the

Caturhotra fire-piling, also with the Mantras for the human sacrifice, for the animal sacrifice for the Brahmamedha.

item.title: ३ Critical Study of subjects
item.description:
[[P030]]

22

The Critical Study of the subjects discussed

1 The Philosophical & Religious Subjects:-

This Aranyaka contains two Upanisads, the Taittiriya and the Narayana; besides these there are many philosophical ideals scattered in the whole Aranyaka. Let us deal with them in various headings:-

Atman, Brahman, Puruss, Aka ara, Paratma, Narayana-

These words have been used for the Supreme Universal Soul. It has been said that Atman was first one, non-second and that is in all beings. “Through fear of him the wind blows, through fear the sun rises, through fear of him Indra and Death move.” (T.A. 8.8.1). Atman is across the water, in the world, at the back of the heaven, greater than the great’. In that supreme and immortal one are all beings. He has pervaded the sky, the heaven, the earth. By him the sun shines.

item.title: ४ The Literery beauty
item.description:
[[P053]]

44

There is some flow and impressing power in the description and the depiction of the matters in this Aranyaka. Many stories have been invented to give impression of any abstract idea. For example we may take the mythology of the Pravargya sacrifice. gods began a great sacrificial sessions Visnu obtained fame in that session. Visnu wished that very much, not to distribute among the gods; he escaped away with that, the gods followed him to check the fame; of him, being followed, the bow was born from the left and the arrows were born from the right; therefore, arrow and bow have pious birth, for they are born of the sacrifice; many gods could not defeat Visnu, who was alone; therefore, many men, having no arrow and bow do not defeat one who has arrow and bow. He laughed, ‘many gods could not defeat me alone’; from him, laughing in pride, the brilliance ran away; the gods hided that in the plants; they became the Syamaks plants having the names Smayakes caused by the laughter. He stood holding firmly his bow on the earth. Those white ants spoke to the gods, “we pray for the boon, we will perform this for you; whenever we dig, may we wet that by the waters; therefore, whenever the white ants dig, they wet that by the waters; for that is chosed by them; they ate even the rope of his (Vienu’s) bow; his bow going forcefully above out and put his head above; that moved following the heaven and the earth.

item.title: ५ CONCLUSION
item.description:
[[P056]]

46

Now we have to discuss the Kandanukrams, the Kalpa Sutras and the Taittiriya Pratisakhya. The Kandanukrama is of the Atreyi Sakha of the Black Yajurveda. The text of the Aranyaka is found discussed in that work along with the Samhita and the Brahmana. There are five Kalpasutras connected with the Taittiriya sakha of the Veda.

These are:-

1. The Baudhayana Srautasutra

2. The Apastamba srautasutra

3. The Hiranyakesi or Satyasadha Srautasutra
